key_insight: Task-aware fusion of complementary structural encoders improves materials property prediction by selecting representations from property-relevant network depths.
engineering_relevance: A lightweight fusion bridge can improve prediction accuracy while reducing trainable parameters and halving overall training time relative to MatterChat.
method: Use task-conditioned latent queries to fuse CHGNet features with intermediate Zatom-1 representations.
Learn representation selection and material–language alignment jointly on downstream tasks, without separate contrastive pretraining.
Optionally incorporate UMA-S as a third structural encoder.
evidence_signal: Across classification and regression tasks, TCAF outperforms MatterChat with up to 47.8% lower RMSE; the three-encoder configuration achieves 89.61% macro-average classification accuracy.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify dataset sizes or evaluation splits, leaving generalization to unfamiliar materials uncertain.
paper_title: Choosing the Right Representations: Task-Aware Fusion for Multimodal Materials Language Models
